description: design-checks 5.5.2 and 5.6 (D-124): the built-in design checks and hints, each a SELECT file in this folder pinned by SHA-256. 'level' is the group's: Problem or Worth a look for the 28 checks (DC-24 is a Problem in a project made under the address pattern, and DC-27 calls an example address Worth a look), Hint for the twelve hints, each phrased as a question. 'sentences' are what each row becomes, by variant, filled by checks.py from the row; 'fix' is the one-sentence fix. 'block' is the part of the Edit form a finding opens at. A hint's word lists (roleWords, quantityWords, unitWords, singularWords, smallWords) are read by checks.py from here. Change a file and its hash together; test_checks.py fails on a mismatch. The functions ss:own and ss:term (urn:semantic-studio:check:) are checks.py's: a term is the document's own unless it is in a standard vocabulary (5.5.1), and ss:term says a subject is typed as a term, never an individual.

checks.heading: Terms without an English label
checks.fix: Add a label in English; other languages are welcome beside it.

checks.heading: Concepts with two preferred labels in one language
checks.fix: Keep one; move the other to alternative labels.

checks.heading: Terms without a definition
checks.fix: Write what it is: the kind of thing, then what sets it apart.

sentences.note: {name} has a note but no definition.

checks.heading: Class names not in UpperCamelCase
checks.fix: Rename in the Edit form or the Turtle editor.

sentences.row: The class {local} is named {local}; class names read {suggested}.

checks.heading: Property names not in lowerCamelCase
checks.fix: Rename in the Edit form or the Turtle editor.

checks.heading: Names holding a version or a date
checks.fix: Names stay the same for ever; versions go in the header.

sentences.date: {local} has a date in its name.
sentences.version: {local} has a version in its name.

checks.heading: Labels copied from the name
checks.fix: Write the label for people, in words; each line suggests one.

checks.heading: Header details missing
checks.fix: Add it in the Edit page's ontology details or the Turtle.

sentences.none: The document has no ontology header.
sentences.title: The ontology has no title.
sentences.creator: The ontology has no creator.
sentences.version: The ontology has no version number.
sentences.semver: The ontology's version {version} is not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
sentences.versionIri: The ontology has no version IRI.

checks.heading: Version IRI does not match the version
checks.fix: The version IRI is the ontology IRI, a slash and the version.

sentences.row: The version IRI ends in {tail} but the version is {version}.

checks.heading: Deprecated terms without a replacement
checks.fix: Name what replaces it, where something does.

sentences.row: {name} is deprecated and names no replacement.

checks.heading: Deprecated terms still in use
checks.fix: Move what uses it to the replacement.

sentences.one: {name} is deprecated but {user} is still one.
sentences.uses: {name} is deprecated but {user} still uses it.
sentences.under: {name} is deprecated but {user} is still under it.

checks.heading: Loops in a hierarchy
checks.fix: Remove one of the links in the loop.

checks.heading: Hierarchies deeper than four levels
checks.fix: Keep four levels until a need shows; say why if it has.

checks.heading: Concepts with more than one broader concept
checks.fix: Keep one parent unless navigation needs two.

checks.heading: Related and broader at once
checks.fix: Keep the one that is true.

sentences.row: {name} is both related to and under {other}.

checks.heading: Concepts in no scheme; schemes with no top concept
checks.fix: Add it to a scheme.

sentences.scheme: The scheme {name} has no top concept.

checks.heading: One label on two terms
checks.fix: Make the labels say how they differ.

checks.heading: Terms already in a reference ontology
checks.fix: Reuse the reference term (Edit offers it) instead of a copy.

checks.heading: Date-times without a time zone
checks.fix: Add Z for UTC or an offset such as +01:00.

checks.heading: Numbers written as text
checks.fix: Store the number with a number type, and the unit apart.

checks.heading: The document imports others
checks.fix: Reuse terms by their address instead; an import brings everything it holds.

checks.heading: Same-as links
checks.fix: Same-as merges two things completely; a close or exact match is weaker and safer.

checks.heading: Both a class and a concept
checks.fix: Keep two linked terms, one of each.

sentences.row: {name} is both a class and a concept.

checks.heading: Individuals in the ontology's namespace
checks.fix: Keep data at a data address: .../data/<data-domain>/<class>/<id>.

checks.heading: Individuals without a label; unused declarations
checks.fix: Add an example, or ask whether it is needed.

sentences.class: {name} is never used by any individual.
sentences.property: {name} is never used by any statement.

checks.heading: Addresses off the pattern
checks.fix: Follow the address pattern in Settings → Naming; existing published addresses stay, new ones follow it.

sentences.type: The ontology's address does not end in -ontology, -taxonomy, -vocabulary, -shapes or -mapping.
sentences.layer: The ontology is not under core/, domain/<domain>/ or app/<application>/.
sentences.term: {name} is not under the ontology's address followed by #.
sentences.class: {name} is at data/…/{found}/ but its most general class is {expected}.

checks.heading: Tool-default or example addresses
checks.fix: Move to your organization's namespace.

sentences.example: The ontology uses an example address ({host}).
sentences.default: The ontology uses an editor's default address.
sentences.termsExample: Terms under {namespace} use an example address ({host}).
sentences.termsDefault: Terms under {namespace} use an editor's default address.

checks.heading: Addresses with capitals, underscores or versions in their path
checks.fix: Path segments are lowercase words joined by hyphens; versions go in the header.

sentences.capital: {whose} address has a capital letter in its path ({segment}).
sentences.underscore: {whose} address has an underscore in its path ({segment}).
sentences.version: {whose} address has a version in its path ({segment}).

checks.heading: Home-made copies of standard terms
checks.fix: Use the standard term each line names; Edit shows how.

checks.heading: Rules that OWL 2 RL reasoning does not use
checks.fix: Keep it if it documents the model; a reasoner in OWL 2 RL will not act on it.

sentences.row: Is {name}'s rule "{rule}" meant for a reasoner? OWL 2 RL, the reasoning Semantic Studio runs, does not use it.

checks.heading: Domains and ranges, which add types
checks.fix: Keep a domain or range that should add the type; to refuse data that breaks it, write a shape.

sentences.domain: Is whatever {verb} something meant to be {a_class}? A domain makes it one; it never refuses data.
sentences.range: Is whatever something {verb} meant to be {a_class}? A range makes it one; it never refuses data.
sentences.inferred: The last reasoning run made {count} {things} {a_class} this way.

checks.heading: Types reasoning gave that nobody wrote
checks.fix: If the type is wrong, look at the domain, range or rule that gave it.

sentences.row: Did you mean {name} to be {a_class}? Reasoning concluded it; nobody wrote it.
sentences.noRun: No current reasoning result: run reasoning in Edit, then Run again.
sentences.noProject: Reasoning runs on a project; this check reads its last run.

checks.heading: Definitions that say anything
checks.fix: Say what kind of thing it is, then what sets it apart.

sentences.row: {name}'s definition says "anything": what sets it apart from everything else?

checks.heading: Definitions that may not define
checks.fix: Write what it is: the kind of thing, then what sets it apart; examples go in skos:example.

sentences.example: Is {name}'s definition a definition, or an example? It says "{word}".
sentences.repeats: Does {name}'s definition say more than its name? It repeats "{label}".
sentences.short: Is {name}'s definition enough to tell it apart? It has {count} {words}.

checks.heading: Acronyms not spelled out
checks.fix: Write the full words once, in the definition or an alternative label.

sentences.row: What does {acronym} stand for in {name}? Spell it out in the definition or an alternative label.

checks.heading: Class names that look plural
checks.fix: Name the class for one member: Mission, not Missions.

sentences.row: Is {name} one thing or many? A class names each of its members, so its name is singular: {singular}.

checks.heading: Roles named as kinds
checks.fix: Make the role a relationship, or say why it is a kind, if the same one can stop playing it.

sentences.row: Is {name} a kind of {parent}, or a role {a_parent} plays for a while? A role is often better as a relationship.

checks.heading: Sibling classes that say the same
checks.fix: Merge them, or give each what sets it apart.

sentences.row: Are {names} different enough to be separate classes? Under {parent} they have the same properties and rules.

checks.heading: Numbers with no unit
checks.fix: Put the unit in the name, the definition or a unit annotation.

sentences.row: What unit is {name} in? Say it, so that two values can be compared.

checks.heading: Text that names another individual
checks.fix: Make it a relationship to the individual, if that is what it means.

sentences.row: Should {property} be a relationship? {subject}'s {property} is the text "{value}", the name of {individual}.

checks.heading: Functional properties
checks.fix: Keep the mark if two values can never both be true; else remove it.

sentences.row: Can {name} ever have two values? It is marked functional, so a reasoner reads two values as one thing, or as a contradiction.
